title: Article III standing
question: Who may sue in federal court?

steps.note: Injury in fact, including aesthetic injury, but to the plaintiff itself.
Injury, causation, redressability; Congress cannot confer standing on everyone.
An informational injury shared widely can still be concrete.
Reasonable concern that deters use of a river is injury; civil penalties can redress.
States get special solicitude; a small contribution to a large harm suffices.
A bare statutory violation is not automatically concrete.
Concrete injury needs a close historical analogue; every class member must have it.
States lack standing to force more arrests and prosecutions.
